tool.name: PharmCAT pharmacogenomics
tool.description: star-allele diplotypes, phenotypes and CPIC/DPWG/FDA recommendations from a germline VCF
tool.command: ## copied, not linked: pharmcat_pipeline resolves links and recognises a VCF by its file extension #if $input.ext == "vcf_bgzip": cp '$input' sample.vcf.bgz && #set $vcf = "sample.vcf.bgz" #else: cp '$input' sample.vcf && #set $vcf = "sample.vcf" #end if ## PharmCAT downloads its reference into its environment on first use; serialise that between concurrent jobs bindir=\$(dirname "\$(command -v pharmcat_pipeline)") && flock "\$bindir/.reference.lock" python -c "import sys, pathlib; from pcat.utilities import download_reference_fasta_and_index as d; p = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); (p / 'reference.fna.bgz.gzi').exists() or d(p)" "\$bindir" && pharmcat_pipeline '$vcf' -o out $absent_to_ref #if $sources: -rs '$sources' #end if -reporterHtml -reporterJson -reporterCallsOnlyTsv -cp \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} && mv out/sample.report.html '$report' && mv out/sample.report.json '$report_json' && mv out/sample.report.tsv '$calls'

param.name: input
param.label: Germline variant calls (VCF, GRCh38)
param.help: One sample, the caller's VCF or the workflow's normalised calls. Chromosomes may be named 1 or chr1.

param.name: absent_to_ref
param.label: Assume pharmacogenomic positions absent from the VCF are reference (0/0)
param.help: Only for a whole-genome or gVCF-like call set. In an exome VCF an absent position is often simply not covered (off-target), and this would turn missing data into a reference call.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Runs PharmCAT 3.4.0 (ClinPGx; Sangkuhl et al. 2020, Li et al. 2025): the VCF preprocessor normalises the calls at PharmCAT's pharmacogenomic positions, the named-allele matcher calls star-allele diplotypes for the genes callable from a VCF (ABCG2, CACNA1S, CFTR, CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP3A4, CYP3A5, CYP4F2, DPYD, F2, F5, G6PD, IFNL3, NAT2, NUDT15, RYR1, SLCO1B1, TPMT, UGT1A1, VKORC1), the phenotyper assigns phenotypes and the reporter lists the CPIC, DPWG and FDA-label recommendations.
Outputs: the PharmCAT HTML report, its JSON, and the calls-only TSV (gene, diplotype, phenotype, activity score, missing positions), which the exome clinical report shows in its pharmacogenomics section.
**Exomes**: positions outside the capture are absent from the VCF and are reported by PharmCAT as missing; a call made with missing positions can hide an allele defined there (e.g. CYP2C19 \*17, UGT1A1 \*28/\*80 promoter). CYP2D6, HLA-A/B and MT-RNR1 need outside calls and are not made here. On the first run PharmCAT downloads its GRCh38 reference (about 0.9 GB) into its conda environment.
PharmCAT is MPL-2.0; its guideline data come from CPIC, DPWG and the FDA via ClinPGx.
